issues.title: Substring-match scan selectivity (minimal, finish E0001)
issues.hypothesis: q09 (123.8ms, slowest template) builds hash joins on orders (1.5M) and partsupp (800k) while the real probe side is about 324k rows. The cause is that the part scan filter contains(p_name,'ghost'), pushed down from LIKE '%ghost%', is estimated at DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY 0.2 (about 40k rows), but only about 5% of rows pass. EXPLAIN shows estimates of about 1.26M rows for lineitem⋈part⋈orders and 5.06M for the top join. E0001 did not fail as an idea: the implementer ran out of time while building, and it was never benchmarked. If the part estimate drops to about 8k, the join-order optimizer should make the filtered part/lineitem side the build side.
issues.plan: Keep the diff small and out of the header, so the rebuild stays short. In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp, add a file-local static helper IsSubstringMatchFilter(const TableFilter&). It returns true for an ExpressionFilter whose expression is contains(col, non-empty VARCHAR constant), or ~~/like_escape with a constant pattern that starts with '%' and contains a literal character. It recurses into ConjunctionAndFilter children. It never matches OR, NOT or !~~. In ExtractGetStats (around lines 146-151), when no equality filter applied and some non-optional table filter matches, use selectivity 0.04 (a file-local constexpr) instead of DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY. Leave relation_manager.cpp unchanged in this experiment. Then: build in the background, EXPLAIN q09.m0 and confirm the part estimate falls to about 8k and the join order changes, then run the full bench.
issues.expected_gain: q09: 20-40% if the build sides flip. Other templates with LIKE '%x%' filters on a dimension table (q13-like, q16, q14 variants) may change their plans. Geomean: 1-3%.
issues.generality: Any query with a substring LIKE or contains filter on a table that is joined. Substring filters are usually much more selective than 0.2. A query whose substring filter matches most rows could get a worse join order, since the estimate would be about 5x too low.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Only estimates change, so results stay correct. Plan changes on hidden templates could regress some. Mitigation if results are mixed: apply the lower selectivity only when the literal is at least 3 characters.

output.memory:
## db_evolve planner memory (duckdb)

### Round log
- G1R1: baseline 1.000x, geomean 40.0ms. Dispatched E0001 "Lower cardinality estimate for substring-match table filters" (q09 join estimates 4-15x too high). Backlog: q13 high-cardinality hash agg investigation.
- E0001 RETIRED, but only because the implementer ran out of time (header change caused a rebuild of more than 10 minutes, and it was never benchmarked). That was a bad implementation process, not a bad idea.
- G1R2: profile geomean 42.1ms (noise against 40.0). Re-dispatched a minimal version, "Substring-match scan selectivity (minimal, finish E0001)": cpp-only, ExtractGetStats path only, relation_manager.cpp untouched.

### Lessons for dispatching
- Keep diffs out of widely included headers (long rebuilds kill the implementer's budget). Use file-local statics or constexpr in the .cpp.
- Ask implementers to run the build in the background and to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench.

### Tooling facts
- `dbe-tool sql "EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) ..."` hung until the 120s timeout. Plain EXPLAIN piped into `grep -oE "HASH_JOIN|[0-9,]+ rows|[a-z_]+ = [a-z_]+"` works and is cheap for estimates.
- Bash: compound commands (;, multiple pipes, cd &&) and redirects to /tmp need approval. Use single commands; use the Read/Grep tools for files (read .dbe files individually).
- profile.md truncates big plans (the q09 lower half and the q18 subquery aggregate are missing). Operator times are summed CPU across threads, not wall time.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- LIKE: src/function/scalar/string/like.cpp already has a LikeMatcher (constant pattern segments, FindStrInStr via memchr in contains.cpp). '%x%' is rewritten to contains. LIKE micro-optimization looks low value.
- FSST string scan (src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp StringScanPartial/Select) decompresses every row. The comment columns are FSST. enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false. Filtering on compressed strings would be a big project.
- Join-order cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 (relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57). It is applied flat to non-equality table filters (relation_statistics_helper.cpp:146-151) and in relation_manager.cpp:199,258,276,293,374. InspectTableFilter (line 446) handles only CONJUNCTION_AND and CONSTANT_COMPARISON equality.
- In q09 the part filter is pushed into the scan as contains(p_name,'ghost'), so the table-filter path is the one that matters. Baseline EXPLAIN: about 1.26M rows estimated for lineitem⋈part⋈orders and 5.06M for the top join.
- Perfect hash agg: CanUsePerfectHashAggregate in src/execution/physical_plan/plan_aggregate.cpp:127, gated by the perfect_ht_threshold setting (don't change defaults).
- Radix HT adaptation: DecideAdaptation in radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424 (SKIP_LOOKUP threshold 0.95), MaybeRepartition at :479.

### Profile hotspots (current best)
- Shares: q09 124ms, q13 110, q18 98, q19 48, q16 45, q22 42, then the rest at 20-35ms.
- q09: two hash joins about 0.22s CPU each, building on orders 1.5M and partsupp 800k while the real probe side is 324k.
- q13: orders scan with NOT LIKE '%a%b%' 0.22s (FSST decompression + match), RIGHT join 0.11s, HASH_GROUP_BY 150k groups 0.20s.
- q18: likely GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING over lineitem (1.5M groups). The plan is truncated in the profile; run `dbe-tool profile q18.m0` next round.

### Directions
- Promising: cardinality estimates (cheap, plan-level, correctness-safe). Watch for regressions on other templates.
- Unexplored: q18 large aggregation, q13 aggregation (backlog issue: profile first), hash join build cost in general, q19 (OR-of-conjunctions filter on part/lineitem).
- Exhausted: none yet.
